system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Template based System Prompts. Install and update Agent Skills, prompt files or Agent definitions.
system_prompt_style.note: Default prompt reads AGENTS.md if present; skills/MCP add sections.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Enter a shell with `!`, or run shell commands e.g. `! cd web && npm run build`.
env_context_strategy.note: Shell/file tools used by the agent to explore; AGENTS.md read is noted.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The default **`fast-agent`** registry contains skills to let you set up LSP, Agent and Tool Hooks, Compaction strategies, Automation and more.
context_compaction.note: Compaction guide shipped (docs/docs/guides/compaction.md); exact defaults not shown in evidence.

observation_format.evidence_quote: For MCP Tool Results, `ImageResources` and `EmbeddedResources` are converted to User Messages and added to the conversation.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Structured Outputs, PDF and Vision support is simple to use and well tested.
tool_call_format.note: Tool calls via provider APIs (MCP tools exposed as function tools); parser file not in evidence.

tool_schema_source.note: MCP-sourced tool schemas are evidenced; whether built-in tools are hand-written or auto-generated is not shown in excerpts. The README places this line under 'Start Here', but no line number is available, so the locator has no line.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: topics: a2a, acp, agent, agent-framework, agent-skills, cli, mcp, mcp-client, mcp-server, python, skills, tui

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Given a complex task, the Orchestrator uses an LLM to generate a plan to divide the task amongst the available Agents.
loop_primitives.note: Default interactive agent is react; orchestrator/MAKER (k-voting) are config-reachable workflows.

planning_granularity.note: Explicit plan objects exist in orchestrator/ACP planner; default shell agent has no plan object.

multi_agent_topology.note: Default `-x` session is a single agent; `-xx` enables built-in subagents, orchestrator/router topologies are config-reachable.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: With child agents exposed as tools, you can implement routing, parallelization, and orchestrator-workers
delegation_mechanism.note: Default single agent has no delegation; subagent_spawn reachable via agents-as-tools / `-xx`.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Tool calls in ACP mode prompt for permission by default. You will see options for Allow Once / Always Allow / Reject Once / Never Allow.
human_in_loop.note: Disable with --no-permissions; agents can also request human input.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Conversations are based on `PromptMessageExtended`, fast-agent's extension of the MCP `PromptMessage` type.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Manage skills with the `/skills` command, and connect to MCP Servers with `/connect`.
long_term_memory.note: Agent Skills (SKILL.md) installed to fast-agent home; AGENTS.md read by default prompt.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Session persistence and resume are disabled.
state_persistence.note: Quote describes --no-home disabling resume, implying resume is default.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Evaluator-Optimizers combine 2 agents: one to generate content (the `generator`), and the other to judge that content and provide actionable feedback (the `evaluator`).
self_verification.note: Config-reachable workflow; default shell agent has none.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: the pair run in a loop until either the evaluator is satisfied with the quality, or the maximum number of refinements is reached
retry_policy.note: Default has no retry; evaluator_optimizer (max_refinements) and MAKER (max_samples) are opt-in.

termination_condition.note: Iteration caps in workflows; default interactive loop ends on user/model turn completion.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Routers use an LLM to assess a message, and route it to the most appropriate Agent.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: If you want commands to run in the fast-agent process instead, use:
execution_isolation.note: Shell mode runs on host; Docker/HF sandbox environments shipped as examples.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Start with `-x` option to enable access to Client terminal
filesystem_access.note: Relative to host boundary; no path allowlist shown.

network_policy.evidence_quote: fast-agent go --url https://hf.co/mcp # with a remote MCP
network_policy.note: No network restriction mechanism appears in the evidence.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Persistent “Always” decisions are stored in the fast-agent home (default `.fast-agent/auths.md`) so you can audit or edit them later.
permission_model.note: Documented for ACP mode; --no-permissions allows all.

tracing.note: OpenTelemetry reference page shipped; not necessarily on by default.

replayability.evidence_quote: Passthrough and Playback LLMs enable rapid development and test of Python glue-code for your applications.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: excellent for use as a Coding Agent, Development Toolkit, Evaluation or Workflow platform.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Disable prompts entirely with `fast-agent-acp --no-permissions` (all tools are allowed).
guardrails.note: Permission store gates tool execution; a privacy_filter guide also ships.

target_domain.note: General MCP tool use is first-class.

open_source.note: Apache/MIT badge shown via pypi license shield; LICENSE file present.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: Model support is comprehensive with native support for Anthropic, OpenAI and Google providers as well as Azure, Ollama, Deepseek and dozens of others via TensorZero.
